headline: Slowed down on purpose: the Rockets can wear Houston's sound if they credit it
summary: Houston music runs on tempo and pride, from DJ Screw's chopped-and-screwed tapes to Travis Scott, Megan Thee Stallion and Don Toliver. Under the hip-hop sit Duke-Peacock blues, Frenchtown zydeco and Tejano. Slab culture, with its candy paint, swangas, wood grain and trunk art, gives the market its richest design vocabulary. The scene respects people who pay it back locally.

insights.title: Slow is the signature
insights.detail: DJ Screw and the Screwed Up Click pioneered chopped and screwed on the Southside in the 1990s. It slows the tempo and stretches the pitch until the music feels heavy and syrupy. It is Houston's most recognizable export, and a mood as much as a genre.
insights.implication: Tell the Rockets story at a slow, heavy, unhurried pace: long gradients, stretched type, blur and smear graphics. Skip speed and aggression.

insights.title: The car is the stage
insights.detail: Slab culture is how Black Houston shows off its music and status: older Cadillacs and Chevys in candy paint, with swangas or elbows, big chrome wheels and trunk displays. It runs from Third Ward Sunday cruising to the Art Car Parade crossover.
insights.implication: Candy paint, chrome and trunk-display graphics are the real materials and finishes for footwear, jerseys and outerwear. Partner with slab builders and clubs instead of imitating them.

insights.title: Two ends of the city, two sounds
insights.detail: The Fifth Ward gave Houston the Geto Boys and Rap-A-Lot, and Duke-Peacock Records before them. The Third Ward and South Park gave it Screw, Lil' Keke, Trae tha Truth and Beyonce. Southwest Alief now drives Maxo Kream and Tobe Nwigwe, with a Vietnamese, Nigerian and Latino mix.
insights.implication: Build drops and community nights for specific neighborhoods (Fifth, Third, Alief) instead of a generic H-Town badge. Name the neighborhoods in the product story.

insights.title: Current stars with Houston on their backs
insights.detail: Travis Scott (Missouri City, Cactus Jack, Astroworld), Megan Thee Stallion of Texas Southern and Hot Girl fame, and Don Toliver keep putting Houston imagery in their work. Rockets games are a regular celebrity-seat scene for the local rap class. On the court, the ketchup-and-mustard throwback and a Durant-Sengun-Thompson lineup give the Rockets their own bridge to the scene.
insights.implication: Keep player-artist content local and collaborative: put Rockets players in these artists' studios and shows. Jordan Brand ties to Cactus Jack mean any Travis crossover needs coordination across Nike and Jordan.

insights.title: Houston's older music is a design archive
insights.detail: Don Robey's Duke-Peacock label and Bronze Peacock club, Lightnin' Hopkins's Third Ward blues, Frenchtown zydeco (Clifton Chenier) and Tejano all produced record sleeves, club posters and typography. They predate rap and rarely show up in sportswear.
insights.implication: A vintage-label, record-sleeve story gives the City Edition a deeper source than the usual space and rocket imagery.

insights.title: Radio and the arena
insights.detail: 97.9 The Box (KBXX), KTSU 90.9 at Texas Southern and KPFT 90.1 carry the city's sound. Toyota Center production is expected to play local anthems and slowed remixes.
insights.implication: Seed products and capsules through Houston radio and DJs (screw-style mixes), as well as player channels.

places.name: Screwed Up Records & Tapes
places.why: DJ Screw's shop, and the pilgrimage site for the Screwed Up Click.

places.name: Toyota Center
places.why: Rockets home, and the stage for the touring rap, R&B and Latin acts that fill the city.

places.name: NRG Stadium and NRG Park
places.why: Home of the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo concert series and the former Astroworld Festival site.

places.name: Warehouse Live
places.why: A long-running mid-size room for hip-hop, rock and local showcases.

places.name: White Oak Music Hall
places.why: A multi-stage indoor-outdoor venue that books rap, indie and Latin acts.

places.name: Cactus Music
places.why: A long-standing independent record store with in-store performances.

places.name: Emancipation Park
places.why: A historic Black community park, and a home for Juneteenth gatherings and local music.

places.name: KTSU 90.9 FM
places.why: The campus station has long backed local hip-hop and jazz.

places.name: The Orange Show Center for Visionary Art
places.why: Organizer of the Art Car Parade and keeper of Houston's outsider-art, car-as-canvas tradition.

people.name: DJ Screw (Robert Earl Davis Jr., d. 2000)
people.role: DJ and originator of chopped and screwed
people.why: Founder of the sound and the Screwed Up Click. Houston honors him every year around his November anniversary.

people.name: Bun B and Paul Wall
people.why: Bun B of UGK, who also runs Trill Burgers, and Paul Wall of grills and Swishahouse are the most visible elders. They regularly turn up for Houston teams.

people.name: Scarface and the Geto Boys / Rap-A-Lot Records
people.role: Fifth Ward rap pioneers and label
people.why: They built Houston's first national rap identity. J. Prince's Rap-A-Lot is still active.

people.name: Travis Scott
people.why: A Missouri City native and the biggest Houston name now. Astroworld is a city symbol, and the 2021 festival tragedy is sensitive history.

people.name: Megan Thee Stallion
people.why: A Houston native and Texas Southern alum, often seen at the city's sporting events.

people.name: Beyonce
people.why: Grew up in Houston's Third Ward and keeps close ties to the city, including Texas Southern and local charities.

people.name: Trae tha Truth
people.why: A South Side figure known for Relief Gang and community aid, and a model for doing this right.

people.name: Maxo Kream and Tobe Nwigwe
people.why: They represent the diverse, immigrant-family Southwest Houston that the generic slab image misses.

moments.name: Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo concert series
moments.why: Houston's largest annual music moment, with country, Tejano, hip-hop and Latin nights at NRG Stadium. It overlaps the Rockets' stretch run.

moments.name: Juneteenth in Third Ward and Fifth Ward
moments.why: Community gatherings and music in historic Black Houston neighborhoods. Texas has a particular claim to the holiday.

moments.name: DJ Screw anniversary tributes
moments.why: Mixes, listening events and community tributes mark his death in November 2000. It is a respectful hook during Cup group play.

moments.name: Houston Art Car Parade
moments.why: Car-as-canvas culture that overlaps with slab imagery, around the playoff window.

moments.name: Rockets home games at Toyota Center
moments.timing: Every home game, Oct to April
moments.why: Arena DJ, halftime and local-artist moments, plus rapper and R&B celebrities in the seats.

vocabulary.meaning: A customized car (the name stands for Slow, Loud and Bangin'). Usually an older American sedan in candy paint, with chrome wheels and a loud sound system.
Wheels that stick out from the car's body. The most visible slab modification.
Slowed, pitched-down remixes with turntable cuts, created by DJ Screw.
DJ Screw's crew, including Lil' Keke, Big Moe, Fat Pat and Z-Ro.
Local shorthand for Houston and its original area code.
A nickname tied to the Rockets' 1994-95 title teams. Fans use it, and it shows up on apparel.
Custom gold or diamond teeth, a Houston staple associated with Paul Wall.
Bun B and UGK's blend of true and real, and a Houston badge of the real thing.

designCues.cue: Candy apple red, the slab paint finish
designCues.source: Slab paint culture, and close to the Rockets red
designCues.use: Deep, glossy red-to-black fades on uppers and jersey panels, with metallic flake finishes.

designCues.source: Slab candy paint and Screw-era tape art
designCues.use: Accent gradients and midsole colors. Avoid any drug reference in the naming.
Mirror-chrome swoosh and hardware, with wheel spokes referenced in the outsoles.

designCues.source: The Rockets' retro red and yellow, per Secret Houston reporting
designCues.use: Pair gold-yellow with candy red for a music-flavored throwback colorway.

designCues.source: Screw tapes and local mixtape covers
designCues.use: Hand-lettered, stretched and slanted display type for hits and graphic tees. Credit the original artists.
Illustrated trunk-scene graphics for tees and hoodies, commissioned from Houston artists.
Peacock-feather and record-label motifs for a heritage capsule. Check rights first.
Metallic gold foils and tooth-like embossing as small details.

productHooks: Slab capsule: candy-red and chrome footwear and a satin bomber with trunk-display graphics, designed with Houston slab builders and artists.
Screwed capsule: slowed-gradient apparel and mixtape-style packaging, with a Rockets playlist produced with Houston DJs and timed to November.
Third Ward and Fifth Ward neighborhood series with named local artists, and a share of proceeds to community groups.
City Edition or throwback tie-in in the ketchup-and-mustard palette, with record-label graphics.
watchouts: Don't use drug references (purple drank, lean) in names or graphics. Real loss shaped the culture.
DJ Screw's name and tape art, and Rap-A-Lot, Swishahouse and Cactus Jack graphics, are third-party IP. They need licenses and estate or label approval.
Astroworld carries the 2021 festival tragedy. Avoid Astroworld branding unless Travis Scott's team leads.
Slab culture belongs to Black Houston. Pay and credit builders and clubs, and don't use it as costume.
